title: EY is creating a 'value realization' office to make sure its AI spending pays off
summary:
The Big Four firm is setting up a new function called the "AI Value Realization Office" to centralize its AI spending and ensure the technology delivers measurable impact.
Its job is to govern AI spending, drive returns, monitor usage, decide which AI initiatives to scale, and oversee how AI reshapes jobs.
However, AI spending and its potential payoff can cut across IT, finance, sales, HR, and operations, said Diasio.
The AI value realization office is the modern-day equivalent, reallocating a set of responsibilities scattered across finance, technology, and other teams to a strategic function in its own right.
Giving AI governance more clout — through a function like the AI value realization office — will be a "critical part" of how EY's clients move forward, said Diasio.

title: Anthropic explains how Claude’s invisible text watermarks will work
summary:
Take the sentence “The weather today was cold and…”.
Watermarking uses low-stakes choices like these—which occur many times over a piece of generated text—to leave a pattern in Claude’s responses.
That pattern is undetectable to the reader, but is detectable to anyone who has a key that encodes it.
When watermarking is used, choices are still made at random, but the source of the randomness is different.
Instead of using an arbitrary random number generator to pick the next word, watermarking uses the key and a few words that come before to settle what word the model should pick.

title: AI isn’t changing how companies work. It’s changing what a company is
summary:
In " The Art of Subtraction ," I argued that companies should question every requirement, remove unnecessary steps, simplify what is left, and only then automate.
That is the difference between adding AI to a company and becoming an AI-first company.
The companies that pull away in this transition will start from a much more difficult question: What work should no longer exist?
AI agents will increasingly observe activity, maintain context, initiate work, and recommend or execute the next best action.
The second will produce a widening gap between companies that appear to be adopting AI and companies that are actually being remade by it.
